messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we need to finalize how we handle request_id + prompt text in OTEL spans before the retention policy refresh on Friday. High-cardinality is spiking our index costs.
Priya: Agreed. Saw a 3x growth in span tags last month, mostly from prompt variations.
Jordan: Can we split the goals: (1) avoid PII, (2) keep enough fidelity for debugging, (3) keep dashboard cardinality sane?
Sam: For (1) we already should delete user.email and user.name. For request_id and prompt text we need a policy (hash vs drop vs sample).
Mateo: Proposal: 
```yaml
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: "user.id"
        action: "delete"
      - key: "request.id"
        action: "hash"
        hashing:
          salt_env: "OTEL_HASH_SALT"
      - key: "prompt.text"
        action: "hash_with_sampling"
        sampling:
          mode: "probabilistic"
          rate: 0.001
```
Kari: That looks reasonable. Hash request.id to preserve trace grouping but avoid index leakage. Sample prompt hashes aggressively. :+1:
Priya: Concern: hashed prompt.text still produces many unique tokens because slight edits => many hashes. Sampling helps but we also want a stable pseudo-fingerprint for regression tests.
Alex: Right — we need two modes: "debug" (higher fidelity, more retention for flagged customers) and "prod" (aggressive minimization). Console should let account admins opt into debug with audit trail.
Jordan: Implementation note: exporter-side should attach a boolean span attribute `telemetry_minimized` so downstream indexers can pick shorter retention/TTL.
telemetry-bot: export: noticed 1.2M spans in last hour, top attr contributors: prompt.text (48%), trace.request_id (20%)
Sam: UX question — how should rollout look? Canary to 5% of requests, then bump if costs acceptable? Or per-tenant toggle?
Kari: Per-tenant toggle + server-side default to minimized. Canary at infra-level for the attribute-processor rollout.
Mateo: For hashing, we should include per-tenant salt prefix: `tenant_id||global_salt` to avoid cross-tenant collisions and allow customer-level opt-outs.
Priya: Also want to add a small deterministic fingerprint for prompts (normalize -> strip whitespace -> lowercase -> then hash). That reduces variance.
Alex: Good call. Add a `normalize_prompt` processor step before hashing. Also add a flag to keep the first N tokens (N=8) for intent grouping — but store those as hashed tokens, not raw text.
Jordan: Example flow: normalize -> token-truncate(8) -> hash_with_salt -> sample_keep(0.001) -> attach telemetry_minimized=true
Sam: Who owns the console change for per-tenant toggles? @Kari?
Kari: I can take console feature spec. Will need API changes from platform to accept `telemetryPolicy` config on tenant objects.
Alex: Platform API: new PATCH /tenants/:id/telemetry-policy body: `{minimize: bool, debug_mode: enum, sample_rate: float}`. Make defaults safe.
Priya: Add acceptance criteria: when minimize=true, prompt.text removed or hashed, user.id removed, request.id hashed. Dashboards must show reduced cardinality within 24h of switching.
Mateo: Ops: add an alert if cardinality delta > 20% after turning minimize=false (to catch accidental wide-open rollouts).
telemetry-bot: plan: will emit `telemetry_policy_change` event to #eng-platform when tenant updates policy
Alex: OK let's draft a short playbook for on-call: how to toggle, what to expect in metrics, rollback steps. I'll write the playbook and post it.
Kari: I'll own the console PR and API contract doc. PR target: EOW.
Jordan: I'll update OTEL processor config and add tests for normalize+hash pipeline.
Sam: I'll put a canary rollout plan in the release ticket.
Priya: Thanks — this should help cut index cost and keep debugging paths for enterprise customers.
Alex: Great. Final decision: default to minimized telemetry, per-tenant opt-in for debug; hashing + normalization + aggressive sampling for prompt text; request_id hashed with salt.
Kari: Noted.
Alex: Closing thread — follow-ups in the ticket #INFRA-982.
